final_recommendation: UBS acquires Credit Suisse with CHF 100B SNB liquidity backstop capped at taxpayer exposure ceiling; CHF 20B pre-positioned Sunday evening for Monday morning withdrawals; non-discretionary draw protocol locked with 60% auto-trigger; Wednesday cost cuts execute as planned; CS continues as standalone operating entity under UBS ownership with full deposit protection.
minority_objections: SNB resisted live draw counter publication, arguing it would telegraph panic to international markets
Wealth client demanded immediate Saturday night statement release rather than waiting for Sunday morning
AT1 rep initially demanded explicit creditor hierarchy protection before AT1 waterfall memo was locked
key_conflicts: Tension between operational speed (60-minute withdrawal processing demand) and legal/operational feasibility (UBS could not guarantee sub-hour processing contractually)
Conflict over transparency: FINMA wanted live draw counter vs SNB's preference for post-execution disclosure
Debate over integration messaging: CS CEO feared 'systems merged' language would trigger run vs Federal Council's need to signal operational unity
key_concessions: Federal Council capped public loss protection at CHF 100B absolute ceiling, forcing UBS to absorb equity and capital risk beyond that
SNB agreed to CHF 20B pre-positioned liquidity (originally resisted immediate overnight activation) to bridge Monday morning withdrawal gap
UBS committed to Wednesday cost cuts with Monday morning announcement despite operational strain of simultaneous deposit outflows
FINMA agreed to non-discretionary draw protocol with zero administrative gate, removing regulatory review step UBS feared
Federal Council agreed CS continues as standalone legal entity and brand through Q2 rather than immediate dissolution
red_lines: CHF 100B taxpayer exposure ceiling - Federal Council stated 'absolute ceiling' and 'won't move past it'
Non-discretionary SNB draws post-acquisition - UBS stated 'that kills the deal' if discretionary gate remained
Zero-delay withdrawal processing Monday morning - multiple participants stated deposit flight would accelerate if any friction visible
Wednesday cost cuts execute as planned - UBS stated 'non-negotiable' and 'no delays, no hedging'
CS continues as operating entity with visible branding - CS CEO stated depositors 'walk' if they read 'dissolution'
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: International market reaction to mid-morning draw execution if 60% trigger fires during trading hours
Operational feasibility of simultaneous 30% deposit outflows, Wednesday cost cuts, and zero-friction branch operations
Legal exposure from announcing cost cuts Monday morning before full operational validation
Weekend media spiral risk from delaying statement to Sunday morning rather than Saturday night release
AT1 holder litigation risk if CHF 20B pre-position sits outside CHF 100B ceiling (raised but not definitively resolved in transcript)
downstream_risk_variables: Actual Monday morning withdrawal velocity (forecast 25-35% but acknowledged as nonlinear and uncertain)
UBS operational capacity to process withdrawals without visible queues or holds
Market interpretation of mid-morning SNB draw execution if it occurs during trading hours
Creditor reaction to weekly loss tracker if losses approach CHF 60-70B by mid-April
Staff and depositor response to Monday morning cost cut announcement alongside rescue statement
uncertainty_notes: The room converged on the acquisition path with detailed liquidity mechanics, but significant operational execution risk remains unresolved: whether UBS can simultaneously process 25-35% deposit outflows, execute Wednesday cost cuts, announce integration Monday morning, and maintain zero visible friction at branches. The 60% auto-trigger for main draw may fire mid-morning during market hours, forcing real-time transparency the room debated but did not fully stress-test. AT1 treatment of CHF 20B pre-position relative to CHF 100B ceiling was raised but not explicitly resolved in transcript.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: UBS CEO R1: 'liquidity alone doesn't move the needle for us on Monday morning' - drove demand for solvency-credible rescue with CHF 100B loss cap and capital support, not just SNB facility
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: Entire meeting structured around UBS acquisition with binding term sheet, 23:00 board vote deadline, CHF 100B loss cap, Wednesday cost cuts - this was the solution path that shaped every concrete decision
marker_evidence.government_support: CHF 100B SNB backstop became binding constraint and red line; Federal Council capped taxpayer exposure as 'absolute ceiling'; non-discretionary draw protocol was precondition for UBS board commitment
marker_evidence.client_flight: Drove CHF 20B pre-position decision, 60% auto-trigger rule, branch messaging protocol, zero-delay withdrawal processing demand, and Monday morning statement timing - shaped multiple operational decisions
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 waterfall memo published to clarify creditor hierarchy and reduce litigation risk; AT1 rep raised impairment sequence and CHF 20B ceiling treatment, but did not force changes to core deal structure
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: FINMA published AT1 waterfall to clarify hierarchy; AT1 rep raised equity vs AT1 impairment sequence, but this informed legal defensibility rather than changing loss allocation or deal terms
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep warned of 'litigation risk' if creditor hierarchy unclear; FINMA responded with waterfall memo to reduce legal exposure, but litigation risk did not constrain core deal terms or CHF 100B ceiling
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: 23:00 UBS board vote deadline, 22:15 FINMA memo deadline, 23:30 statement release, and repeated references to 'before Monday' drove concrete timing decisions and forced real-time protocol locks
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Drove Sunday statement timing, branch messaging protocol, CHF 20B pre-position, 60% auto-trigger, real-time comms plan for mid-morning draw execution, and Wednesday cost cut announcement timing
